target_customer: Consumers and hobbyists who want a low maintenance pet jellyfish for the desk or home
problem: Jellyfish need specialized tanks with circular flow that keeps them off filter intakes, so they were hard for ordinary pet owners to keep. Jellyfish Art sold designed tanks, live jellyfish and food as a kit.
business_model: Direct to consumer e-commerce of aquarium hardware plus live animals and consumables, sold only through its website
product_category: Consumer hardware and live pet e-commerce

founders.name: Alex Andon
founders.background_notes: YC page lists his later role as Product Management Lead at Meta. A search summary says he began after a 2009 layoff; prior employer not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Required a custom Kreisel shaped acrylic tank, flow design and live animal shipping logistics, which is hard hardware and perishable fulfillment for two people.

defensibility.rationale: The tank design and its press and Kickstarter attention gave an early lead, but the Kreisel concept was a known aquarium design that others could copy; later competitors such as Cubic Orbit and JellyTank appeared.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large aquarium or pet retailer copied or bought it in the sources found. Reef Builders later covered rival jellyfish tanks (Cubic Orbit 20, JellyTank 2017).

market_need_then: The 2011 Kickstarter and press coverage by Gizmodo, Laughing Squid and Gizmag showed consumer curiosity, and the product won a 2011 Global Pet Expo award per one source. Total market size was not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses jellyfishart.com; the YC page also calls it the flagship site of AnyVivo. Acquisition history of the domain not found.

identity.mascot_or_character: Live moon jellyfish are the product itself
identity.visual_style: Design led desktop aquarium with an RGB LED system
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful pet like framing; the current site promises a 3 day Arrive Alive Guarantee

branding.brand_signature: The Desktop Jellyfish Tank and the Arrive Alive Guarantee
branding.community_and_virality: Wide 2011 coverage by Gizmodo, Laughing Squid, Gizmag, Core77 and Make; a 2015 Kickstarter reportedly raised over $100K in three days per AquaNerd.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press pull and repeat Kickstarter success in a niche category, though the name is a generic description and no wider community was found.

outcome_analysis: Jellyfish Art turned a design led desktop tank into a niche e-commerce business, funded by Kickstarter in 2011 and again in 2015 rather than venture capital. YC lists it as inactive and one aggregator says it was acquired in 2014, yet a site under the same name is operating in Florida, so the YC status and the real outcome conflict. The cause of any closure is not public, and no failure factor is supported by a source.
notes: YC marks the company inactive and its page text says acquired in 2014, but only one aggregator supports an acquisition and the buyer is not named, so exit type is unknown. The website jellyfishart.com is live and describes a Fort Lauderdale store, which conflicts with the San Francisco warehouse on the YC page. The 2011 Kickstarter pledge total is reported differently (about $43K and over $60K) so the amount is null; the 2015 figure is as reported by AquaNerd and treated as a floor. No venture round was found. No competitor with a source dated near early 2012 was found; Cubic Orbit and JellyTank appeared later.
